statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail eases three points to 21% after the Nasdaq-100 retraced a new session low: NQ futures trade 30,635.25, about 106 points above a 30,529.25 low, and the cash index at 30,390.15 is only 0.06% under its 30,408.50 previous close against -0.18% an hour earlier. The 10-year Treasury yield has backed off its 5.34% peak to roughly 5.30%. Offsetting amplifiers keep Stress at 78%: VIX sits at a 17.59 session high, up 7.67%, WTI is $92.61 and Brent $101.70.
recommendation: Tail moves to 21% and sits mid watch band. The decisive change since the previous publication is that price made a new session low and then retraced a meaningful portion of it rather than extending, which is direct evidence that mean reversion is still functioning; the 10-year easing from its 5.34% peak points the same way. Under this contract that permits Tail to fall even while the environment stays difficult. It remains difficult: the 622-point NQ session range, a VIX at its session high, WTI 2.42% firmer and Brent 3.74% higher on constrained Chinese refined-fuel supply are genuine amplifiers, and conflicting evidence of this kind raises Stress rather than Tail. Stress is 78% and Confidence 88%. The narrow danger window covers the current hour and the next while price remains below the previous close with volatility at session highs.
headline: Tail eases to 21% as a new session low is retraced and the 10-year backs off its 5.34% peak; Stress holds at 78%
body: The observed Nasdaq-100 picture has improved modestly since the previous publication. At the 14:26Z cutoff an hour ago NQ futures traded 30,626.50-30,648.75 with a 30,590.00 session low and the cash index was 30,352.41, down 0.18%. Since then price extended lower, setting a new NQ low of 30,529.25 and a new cash low of 30,274.65, and then retraced. At the 15:26Z cutoff NQ futures are 30,635.25, down 0.21% on the day but roughly 106 points off that low, and the cash index is 30,390.15, down only 0.06% against a 30,408.50 previous close. That sequence matters more than the net change: a new extreme was made and then rejected, which is the signature of a functioning retracement rather than of the persistent no-pullback path this assessment is designed to detect. The rates channel supports the same conclusion. The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.338% earlier today, its highest since April 2002, but has since eased to roughly 5.28-5.30% with the 2-year near 4.82% and the 30-year around 5.63-5.64%. The acute post-ISM repricing that drove the morning fade has therefore lost intensity. The ISM Manufacturing report released at 14:00Z remains the session's defining macro input: the headline PMI was 54.5 against 54.6 in August and a consensus near 55, a ninth consecutive month of expansion, with New Orders improving to 55.3, Employment to 52.7 and Production easing to 56.7. The market-moving component was Prices at 77.9, up 6.8 points from 71.1 and well above an expected 72, which reinforced an already hawkish rates channel. Earlier releases pointed the same way: initial jobless claims were 197K against a 200K consensus, continuing claims 1,701K, and construction spending rose 0.9%. Energy is the other standing amplifier. WTI is $92.61, up 2.42%, and Brent is $101.70, up 3.74%, after PetroChina withheld gasoline and jet fuel shipments to preserve domestic reserves, tightening refined-fuel availability in a market already disrupted by the blocked Strait of Hormuz and the unresolved US-Iran standoff. That is a persistent background condition rather than fresh escalation today, so it informs Stress rather than Tail. Volatility conflicts with the price recovery: VIX is 17.59, up 7.67% and at its session high, having ranged 16.21-17.59. A volatility index at its high while the index recovers off its low is exactly the kind of conflicting evidence this contract routes into Stress and not into the Tail score. Micron's record fiscal fourth quarter, reported before this session with revenue of $54.23 billion, non-GAAP EPS of $33.42, an 87.0% gross margin and fiscal-Q1 guidance of $61.5 billion plus or minus $1.5 billion, continues to cut against the cautious tape at the sector level. Taken together: Tail 21%, inside the watch band and three points lower; Stress 78%, unchanged and still high; Confidence 88% on fresh verified index, futures, yield, volatility and energy levels plus a verified release calendar. Dominant mode stays mixed. The shared Finviz context file was 40 hours old with a partial collection status and no futures coverage, so it was treated as unhealthy under the inherited contract and contributed nothing to this assessment.

lookbackSummary: Across the preceding 24 hours Claude published an unbroken watch-band regime with a single orange hour. Tail ran between 20% and 25%, touching the 25% block threshold once in the 06:00Z hour on a trend-up reading before easing back when that structure failed to persist, then rising to 24% in the 14:00Z hour as the US cash open reversed the overnight rally. Stress climbed steadily from 72% to 78%, its highest reading of the window, and Confidence was stable at 87-89% throughout. Dominant mode was mixed in 22 of the 24 hours. The sequence describes a market absorbing a high-rates, high-energy-price environment inside a wide range rather than trending through it, and the current retracement off a new session low is measured against that baseline.
outlookSummary: The near path turns on whether the retracement off the 30,529.25 NQ low extends back toward the 30,408.50 cash previous close or whether that low is broken without a pullback. Conditional Tail holds at 21% for the current and next hour while those two levels bracket price, eases to 20% through the thinner US midday, ticks back to 21% for the 19:00Z power hour on late-session continuation or reversal risk, then decays to 17-19% across the post-close and Asian hours as liquidity thins and the assumed regime becomes quiet consolidation. From the 05:00Z European handover the conditional path rebuilds to 20-22% on calendar proximity rather than observed structure, ahead of the September employment report at 12:30Z on 2 October. For the release hour and the two hours after it, conditional Stress moves into the extreme band at 80-82% while conditional Tail is capped at 23-24%, one point below the block threshold: under this contract surprise magnitude and forecast dispersion raise Stress, not Tail, until an observed path actually shows failed retracements and repeated extension. No release outcome is assumed anywhere in the forecast.
